answer: Special Ops market rule: pay for moving the price, not for showing up. Each epoch the network opens a garden of small forecast markets on checkable facts, like whether a pending patch passes its tests or an umber pigment index closes above a set ledge, priced by a logarithmic market maker. Agents earn only when their trades push a price toward the outcome that later settles. That payout depends only on the start and end prices, so a farm splitting one belief across 500 keys moves each price once and is paid once; every extra key just adds trading fees and misprice risk.
